A.domain: Arithmetic with rational numbers (subtracting fractions and mixed numbers)

skills.name: Convert mixed numbers to improper fractions
skills.definition: Rewrite a mixed number as an equivalent improper fraction by converting the whole part into fractional units and adding the numerator.
inclusion_criteria: A step explicitly converts a mixed number (e.g., 3 1/2) into an improper fraction (e.g., 7/2)
A step rewrites a mixed number as whole + fraction and then combines into a single fraction
exclusion_criteria: Only rewriting a whole number as a fraction with a chosen denominator (tag S03 instead)
Only converting an improper fraction to a mixed number (tag S06 instead)

skills.name: Find and use a common denominator (LCM/scaling)
skills.definition: Determine a common denominator for two fractions (often via LCM) and create equivalent fractions by scaling numerators and denominators.
inclusion_criteria: A step states or implies finding a common denominator/LCM
A step converts both fractions to equivalent forms with the same denominator
exclusion_criteria: Denominators are already equal and the step directly subtracts numerators (tag S04 instead)
Only rewriting a whole number to match a denominator (tag S03 instead)

skills.name: Rewrite a whole number as an equivalent fraction
skills.definition: Express an integer as a fraction with a specified denominator to enable fraction operations (e.g., 3 = 15/5).
inclusion_criteria: A step rewrites an integer as k/k or as an equivalent fraction with a target denominator (e.g., 2 = 16/8)
exclusion_criteria: Converting a mixed number to an improper fraction (tag S01 instead)
Finding a common denominator between two non-integer fractions (tag S02 instead)

skills.name: Subtract fractions with a common denominator
skills.definition: Compute the difference of two fractions that share a denominator by subtracting numerators and keeping the denominator.
inclusion_criteria: A step performs subtraction in the form a/b − c/b = (a−c)/b
A step subtracts after converting to a common denominator (the subtraction operation itself)
exclusion_criteria: The step is only about finding/converting to a common denominator (tag S02 instead)
The step is only about simplifying/reducing the result (tag S05 instead)

skills.name: Simplify a fraction to lowest terms
skills.definition: Reduce a fraction by dividing numerator and denominator by a common factor and/or recognizing when it is already in lowest terms.
inclusion_criteria: A step explicitly simplifies a fraction (e.g., −3/12 = −1/4)
A step states the fraction is already in lowest terms
exclusion_criteria: Converting an improper fraction to a mixed number without reduction (tag S06 instead)
Performing the subtraction operation itself (tag S04 instead)

skills.name: Convert an improper fraction to a mixed number
skills.definition: Rewrite an improper fraction as a mixed number by dividing the numerator by the denominator and expressing the remainder as a fraction.
inclusion_criteria: A step explicitly converts a/b (with a>b) into a mixed number form
exclusion_criteria: Converting mixed to improper (tag S01 instead)
Only simplifying/reducing a fraction (tag S05 instead)

C.domain: Arithmetic with rational numbers (subtracting fractions and mixed numbers)

skills.name: Convert mixed numbers to improper fractions
skills.definition: Rewrite a mixed number as an equivalent improper fraction by multiplying the whole part by the denominator and adding the numerator.
inclusion_criteria: A solution step explicitly rewrites a mixed number (e.g., 3 1/2) into an improper fraction (e.g., 7/2).
A step rewrites a nonstandard mixed form like 2 3/2 into a sum and then an improper fraction.
exclusion_criteria: Only rewriting a whole number as a fraction with a chosen denominator (tag S03 instead).
Only converting an improper fraction to a mixed number (tag S06 instead).

skills.name: Find a common denominator (LCM) and create equivalent fractions
skills.definition: Determine a common denominator (often via LCM) and convert each fraction to an equivalent fraction with that denominator.
inclusion_criteria: A step states or implies finding a common denominator/LCM for two denominators.
A step shows scaling numerators/denominators to express fractions over the common denominator.
exclusion_criteria: Denominators are already equal and the step directly subtracts numerators (tag S04 instead).
Only rewriting a whole number with a specific denominator (tag S03 instead).

skills.name: Rewrite a whole number as an equivalent fraction
skills.definition: Express an integer as a fraction with a specified denominator (e.g., 3 = 15/5) to enable fraction operations.
inclusion_criteria: A step explicitly rewrites an integer as k/k-denominator form (e.g., 2 = 6/3, 4 = 12/3).
A step chooses a denominator to match another fraction’s denominator.
exclusion_criteria: Converting a mixed number to an improper fraction (tag S01 instead).
Finding a common denominator between two non-integer fractions (tag S02 instead).

skills.name: Subtract fractions using a common denominator
skills.definition: Compute the difference of two fractions by subtracting numerators over a shared denominator (including the already-same-denominator case).
inclusion_criteria: A step performs subtraction after expressing both quantities with the same denominator (e.g., 20/12 − 9/12).
A step uses the rule (a/b − c/b) = (a−c)/b.
exclusion_criteria: The step is only about finding/creating the common denominator (tag S02 or S03 instead).
The step is only simplifying the resulting fraction (tag S05 instead).

skills.name: Simplify a fraction to lowest terms
skills.definition: Reduce a fraction by dividing numerator and denominator by a common factor and/or recognizing it is already in lowest terms.
inclusion_criteria: A step explicitly reduces a fraction (e.g., −3/12 = −1/4).
A step states the fraction is already in lowest terms.
exclusion_criteria: Only converting between mixed and improper forms without reduction (tag S06 instead).
Only performing the subtraction arithmetic (tag S04 instead).

skills.name: Convert an improper fraction to a mixed number (or whole number)
skills.definition: Rewrite an improper fraction as a mixed number (or integer) by dividing the numerator by the denominator and expressing the remainder as a fraction.
inclusion_criteria: A step explicitly converts an improper fraction to a mixed number (e.g., 7/4 = 1 3/4).
A step identifies a fraction equals a whole number (e.g., 3/3 = 1).
exclusion_criteria: Converting mixed to improper (tag S01 instead).
Only simplifying a fraction without converting to mixed form (tag S05 instead).

B.domain: Arithmetic with rational numbers (subtracting fractions and mixed numbers)

skills.name: Convert mixed numbers to improper fractions
skills.definition: Rewrite a mixed number as an equivalent improper fraction by converting the whole part to fractional units and adding the numerator.
inclusion_criteria: A step explicitly converts a mixed number (e.g., 3 1/2) into an improper fraction (e.g., 7/2)
A step rewrites a mixed number as whole + fraction and then combines into a single fraction
exclusion_criteria: Only converting a whole number to a fraction with a chosen denominator (tag S03 instead)
Only converting an improper fraction to a mixed number (tag S06 instead)

skills.name: Find and use a common denominator (LCM/scaling)
skills.definition: Determine a common denominator for two fractions (often via LCM) and create equivalent fractions by scaling numerators/denominators.
inclusion_criteria: A step states or implies finding a common denominator/LCM
A step converts fractions to equivalent forms with the same denominator (e.g., 5/3 = 20/12)
exclusion_criteria: Denominators are already equal and the step directly subtracts numerators (tag S04 instead)
Only rewriting a whole number with a specific denominator (tag S03 instead)

skills.name: Rewrite whole numbers as equivalent fractions
skills.definition: Express an integer as an equivalent fraction with a specified denominator to enable fraction operations.
inclusion_criteria: A step rewrites an integer as k/kden (e.g., 2 = 6/3, 4 = 12/3, 2 = 16/8)
exclusion_criteria: Converting a mixed number to an improper fraction (tag S01 instead)
Finding a common denominator between two non-integer fractions (tag S02 instead)

skills.name: Subtract fractions with a common denominator
skills.definition: Compute the difference of two fractions that share a denominator by subtracting numerators and keeping the denominator.
inclusion_criteria: A step performs subtraction after denominators are made equal (e.g., 20/12 − 9/12)
A step uses the 'same denominator, subtract numerators' rule
exclusion_criteria: The step is primarily about creating common denominators (tag S02 instead)
The step is primarily simplifying/reducing the result (tag S05 instead)

skills.name: Simplify fractions to lowest terms
skills.definition: Reduce a fraction by dividing numerator and denominator by a common factor (including recognizing when it is already simplified).
inclusion_criteria: A step explicitly reduces a fraction (e.g., −3/12 = −1/4)
A step states a fraction is already in lowest terms
exclusion_criteria: Only converting improper to mixed number without reduction (tag S06 instead)
Only performing subtraction without any reduction/simplification claim (tag S04 instead)

skills.name: Convert improper fractions to mixed numbers (or whole numbers)
skills.definition: Rewrite an improper fraction as a mixed number (or integer) by dividing the numerator by the denominator and expressing the remainder as a fraction.
inclusion_criteria: A step converts a result like 7/4 into 1 3/4
A step converts a fraction like 6/5 into 1 1/5
exclusion_criteria: Converting mixed to improper (tag S01 instead)
Only simplifying a fraction without expressing it as a mixed number (tag S05 instead)

skills.name: Subtract mixed numbers by separating whole and fractional parts
skills.definition: Compute a mixed-number difference by subtracting whole parts and fractional parts (including handling a negative fractional difference) and recombining.
inclusion_criteria: A step sets up subtraction as (whole difference) + (fraction difference), e.g., (4−2) + (4/12−7/12)
A step recombines the whole and fractional results into a single value
exclusion_criteria: The method is to convert both mixed numbers to improper fractions first (tag S01 + S04 instead)
Only subtracting two fractions without whole parts (tag S04 instead)
